ModMetaData.name: Armory
ModMetaData.author: Kruecke
ModMetaData.description:
Armory is a weapon inspector and automatic manager for RimWorld 1.6. It shows what every colonist wants to carry, why they are not carrying it, and what the colony should craft, research or buy next.
Every free colonist gets range-aware rankings based on RimWorld's real accuracy curve, plus a ranged role (CQB, Assault, Line or Marksman) that can be overridden per colonist. Armory also assigns a hand type: Ranged or Melee. Simple Sidearms' primary mode wins when present; otherwise an explicit per-colonist choice wins, then a bonded weapon, a ranged-blocking shield belt, Brawler, shooting/melee passion, and finally skill. Only weapons of that hand type compete, so melee and ranged are never compared, and a colonist holding the wrong type is automatically switched to the best ready weapon of the chosen type unless a bonded weapon locks the hand. With Simple Sidearms, Armory models one opposite-type Sidearm 1 and an optional ranged Sidearm 2 chosen to cover a real range gap. It reconciles the carried set, drops duplicates and extras, keeps Simple Sidearms' default/preferred hand aligned with the Armory hand through SS's own API, and does not fight a sidearm Simple Sidearms has temporarily drawn. Blockers stay visible instead of hiding candidates: forbidden, outside the allowed area, unreachable, reserved, biocoded, role restrictions, ideoligion dislike, and Simple Sidearms slot or mass limits.
The Upgrades tab lists every obtainable weapon variant that would improve a colonist, grouped into Craft, Research and Buy. Stuffable weapons are split by material, so a steel knife and a plasteel knife are separate rows with their own score, per-copy material cost, base market value and owned count, and the Craft button queues the bill for that material and names it Armory: Uranium mace (for example) so it stands out from ordinary recipe bills. It shows owned and missing copies, expected gain and the best bench, and can queue one bill when a built bench can make the missing weapon. The Weapons tab compares loose weapons with raw DPS, generic DPSA, armor penetration, separate sortable accuracy columns, base market value in silver and role filters; its detail view shows the best colonist per role. The Colonists tab shows each pawn's Hand, Sidearm 1 and Sidearm 2 lines, status and ranked alternatives. Double-click a colonist or loose weapon row to close Armory and jump to it on the map.
When no other weapon manager is active, automatic weapon management is on by default. Armory queues equip jobs for the best ready weapon, claims each weapon for one pawn, respects a swap cooldown, never unforbids anything, and treats unbonded persona weapons as manual-only. With Simple Sidearms, sidearm management keeps one legal opposite-type Sidearm 1, adds a useful ranged Sidearm 2 when Simple Sidearms has room, drops duplicates and extra sidearms, and upgrades one slot at a time. It uses Simple Sidearms' own intentional-drop API so a removed sidearm is not retrieved in a loop, and it counts current and queued jobs as busy so a resting colonist cannot accumulate duplicate pickup orders. Automatic equipping and sidearm management can each be disabled in settings, and the Log tab records every decision with its reason. A persistent, rolling diagnostic log in ArmoryLogs records decisions and map-load snapshots for troubleshooting.
Simple Sidearms support is optional and read through reflection, so Armory still works without it. No Harmony dependency.
Steam Workshop: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3842538224 Source and issues: https://github.com/fklemme/Armory
